title: Recasting XENONnT and PandaX-4T to inelastic dark matter: the exclusion they could publish tomorrow
question: If XENONnT (3.1 t yr) and PandaX-4T (1.54 t yr) extended their NR analyses to 270-300 keV with LZ-like efficiency and saw 0 or 1 events, what 90% CL limits / discovery significance would they obtain in the (delta, sigma_n) plane for inelastic O1 at 1 TeV, how do these compare with LZ's two-sided interval and P021's likelihood peak, and what does the existing XENON1T 2018 inelastic limit (Fig. S7, to delta = 231 keV) already exclude?
headline_result: Zero events in a 270 keV extension set kappa < 2.11 (XENONnT) or 1.41 (combined) x LZ's one-event coupling, i.e. sigma_SI < 3.3e-42 cm^2 at delta = 300 keV (2.3-6x below LZ's upper edge) but removing only the upper 15%/27% of LZ's 90% interval in ln kappa at every delta; LZ's best fit survives (1.63 expected, P(0) = 0.195); one XENONnT event would be 4.6-5.2 sigma combined and its energy fixes delta to +-15 keV; XENON1T 2018 lies 11-1e5 x above LZ's upper edge and excludes nothing
model_or_mechanism: xenon-target universality; WimPyDD O1 isoscalar inelastic (LZ unit coupling), Sun-frame Baxter SHM (+12-day annual bracket); LZ-like / high-edge / hard-edge efficiencies; Poisson and Feldman-Cousins limits with exposure-scaled LZ backgrounds; sigma_SI = kappa mu_N^2/(pi m_v^4); joint observed-energy extended likelihood LZ + one XENONnT event; Fig. S7 curve endpoints as ROI-edge kinematics
confidence: medium - exposure ratios and kinematics exact; other TPCs' high-energy acceptance/backgrounds assumed; halo tail x10 above 360 keV
